findings.title: consolidate.py is described as present/pending across three sections but was already deleted
locations: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:135 — "there is no Python (the one transitional exception is D8's `consolidate.py`)."

docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:448-455 — "The one transitional Python file is `consolidate.py`… is BYTE-COMPARED against it… the Python is deleted in the same commit that passes it… This is the riskiest single port in the plan and is scheduled with the fallback in hand."
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:956-958 — repository-layout entry listing `consolidate.py` under `src/CLI/` as a file that still exists

src/CLI/Consolidate.jl:2-4 — "ACCEPTANCE (1.6) PASSED 2026-09-09: byte-equal output to the Python on a real PF build (18 pages) and a real IT build (22 pages), all four manuscripts; the Python was deleted in that commit."
findings.description: D1, D8 and the §3 repository-layout tree present `consolidate.py` as a currently-existing transitional Python file with an open, risky, future port ('is scheduled with the fallback in hand', 'is deleted in the same commit that passes it' — future tense). The actual source's own comment in src/CLI/Consolidate.jl records the acceptance test as PASSED on 2026-09-09 and the Python file already deleted in that commit; no .py file exists anywhere in the repository outside .gbg/. The document's own Revision 9 note (line 2498, dated 2026-09-09, same day) even refers to '1.6 acceptance' as an already-measured past event, so the main body (D1/D8/§3) is stale relative to both the code and the document's own revision history. This is exactly the stale-future/deferred claim RULE.DOC.CURRENT forbids ('No stale future, deferred or none-exist claims').
findings.resolution_hint: Rewrite D1 (line 135), D8 (lines 448-455) and the §3 file-tree entry (lines 956-958) in past tense: note that the Gumbo/AbstractTrees port of the consolidator passed its byte-comparison acceptance test on 2026-09-09 and consolidate.py was deleted in that commit, so the tool now has zero Python anywhere (not 'one transitional exception'); remove the `consolidate.py` row from the §3 tree.

findings.title: D9's 'minimal' dependency enumeration omits Pkg and Random, both real hard dependencies
locations: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:559-563 — "The tool declares its own `[deps]`/`[compat]` minimally: the stdlibs `TOML`, `SHA`… `Dates` and `Test`, plus `JSON3`… and `Gumbo` + `AbstractTrees`… both hard dependencies"
Project.toml:6-15 — `[deps]` lists `Pkg` and `Random` in addition to the six named in the architecture text
findings.description: The paragraph enumerates the package's dependency set as if exhaustive ('minimally: the stdlibs TOML, SHA…, Dates and Test, plus JSON3… and Gumbo + AbstractTrees'), but Project.toml also declares `Pkg` and `Random` as hard dependencies, and both are load-bearing: `Pkg.dependencies()` is the mechanism behind `PIN.SELF`/`PIN.TREESHA`/`self verify` that this very document describes at length in D3 and §7.3, and `Random.RandomDevice()` generates the 128-bit pass nonce central to D10's staleness mechanism. A reader following RULE.DOC.CURRENT's bar ('a summary that names only a subset of what the code now provides is stale even if literally true') would be misled about the tool's actual stdlib footprint.
findings.resolution_hint: Add `Pkg` (self-verify / pin checks) and `Random` (pass nonce generation) to the dependency list in D9's paragraph.
